summary: Leo M. Pruden was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1964–1966) and under Akira Hirakawa and Taitetsu Unno. He taught at Brown University (1970–1971), the Nyingma Institute, and the University of Oriental Studies.

Leo Meyer was a linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and at the University of Berlin under Jacob Grimm, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Göttingen and the University of Tartu.

Leo Strauss was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Marburg, and Columbia. His academic career included posts at Cambridge, Columbia, The New School (~1938–1949), the University of Chicago (~1949–1969), Claremont McKenna College, and St. John's College (~1969–1973).
Leon Hurvitz was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He served as a professor at the University of Washington (~1955–1971) and subsequently at the University of British Columbia (~1971–1989).

Linguist Leonard Bloomfield studied at Harvard, Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago under Francis Asbury Wood, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Cincinnati, Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), the University of Chicago (1927–1940), and Yale University (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé is a historian and sinologist. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1965 to 1970 and later held an academic post there from 1998 to 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder and F. E. L. Priestley. He held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).

Leonard Swidler was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who earned degrees from Marquette, Wisconsin-Madison, and Tübingen. He held posts at Duquesne University (1960–1966) and served as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).
Leonard Woolley was an archaeologist and historian. He was educated at St John's School, Leatherhead (~1893–1899) and New College (~1899–1903).
Leonard Zwilling is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Ngawang Wangyal and completed his studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1976.

Leonard van der Kuijp is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. and D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at the University of Washington (~1987–1995) and Harvard University (from 1995).

Leopold Pospisil studied at Charles University in Prague, Willamette University, the University of Oregon, and Yale University. He served as a professor at Yale University from 1956 and as an anthropology curator at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (~1956–1993).

Leopold von Schroeder studied Indology and religion at Tartu under Leo Meyer, and at Leipzig, Jena, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Tartu (1882–1890s), Innsbruck (1896), and the University of Vienna (from 1899).

Leslie S. Kawamura was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Günther. He spent his career at the University of Calgary, serving from circa 1976 to 2010.

Levi McLaughlin is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone. He held posts at Kokugakuin University, Singapore, Iowa, and became associate professor at North Carolina State University (2012).
Lewin Bentham Bowring was an Indologist and historian who served as the Chief Commissioner of the Government of Mysore from circa 1862 to 1870 and held a post at the University of Mysore.

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He held research and teaching posts at the British Museum, Free University of Berlin, Munich, and the University of Bonn.

Lewis Hodous was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Case Western Reserve, Hartford International University, and Halle-Wittenberg. He served as president of Foochow Union Theological School (1902–1917) and professor at Hartford International University (1917–1945).

Lewis Lancaster studied at Roanoke, Claremont, and Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1967–2002) and as president and professor emeritus at the University of the West (1992).

id: P:Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk
summary: Lha Zang Lama Rigdzin Gar Gyi Wangchuk studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
